A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DDO research work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, proofs, and appendices are available and support reliable comparison after matching relocated and renumbered content.

before.justification: v1 reports original DDO finetuning experiments on diffusion and autoregressive models, including FID/IS results, hyperparameter analyses, and generated samples.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds ImageNet 512×512 results, sampling comparisons, and a continued-MLE training control.

M1.justification: The likelihood-ratio objective, diffusion approximation, self-play updates, and VAR adaptation are retained. v2 adds optional inference combinations using DPM-Solver-v3 and autoguidance with DDO-finetuned EDM2-L (Section 5.2 and Table 3); the DDO training procedure itself is unchanged.

E1.justification: v2 extends class-conditional ImageNet generation to 512×512 resolution. This adds a higher-resolution generation scenario while retaining the existing CIFAR-10 and ImageNet populations, domains, and unconditional/class-conditional tasks.

E2.justification: The retained ImageNet 256×256 comparison expands substantially: v2 Table 4 adds methods including ADM-U, SiT+REPA, LightningDiT, MaskGIT, MAR-H, MaskBit, RQ-Transformer, RAR-XXL, and xAR-H. Tables 1–2 remove CAF and GDD-I; Table 2 also adds R3GAN and removes DDPM. These are changes to reported comparator membership, beyond extending comparisons to 512×512.

E3.justification: v2 adds a 512×512 training protocol with 28 rounds and batch size 2048, autoguidance and 25-evaluation sampling configurations, batch-one H100 latency measurements, and OpenCV downsampling for the 256×256 comparison. It also introduces the continued-MLE control. Earlier training settings and 50k-image FID evaluation remain; ImageNet class balancing was already disclosed in v1 Table 2.

E4.justification: Figure 6(b,c) adds continued training with the original diffusion/MLE loss as a control against DDO's hyperparameter sweeps. Table 3 additionally examines the effects of autoguidance and faster sampling on high-resolution generation. Existing hyperparameter, multi-round, and VAR guidance analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates and training curves without independent-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The added experiments do not introduce uncertainty-reporting procedures.

E6.justification: v2 newly reports 512×512 EDM2-L FIDs of 1.96 before finetuning, 1.26 with DDO, and 1.21 with DDO plus autoguidance; the 25-evaluation configuration reports 1.29/1.21. It adds downsampled results, comparator entries, and the MLE-continuation finding. Table 1 changes VDM's CIFAR-10 FID from 4.00 to 7.41, while the original DDO headline scores remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Section 3.4 adds a formal extension through the variational representation of f-divergences and the density-ratio optimum T*=f'(p/q). Theorems 3.1–3.3 and their Appendix B proofs retain the same mathematical content, with equation renumbering.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction extend the guidance-free record-FID claim to ImageNet 512×512 and explicitly describe exploiting reverse KL and self-generated negative signals. The central DDO contribution and earlier diffusion/VAR performance claims are retained.

C2.justification: Section 3.4 adds an RL-based interpretation of self-generated negative signals. Section 5.2 attributes continued-MLE failure partly to an already optimized model and more fundamentally to forward KL, while acknowledging the optimizer-state issue. Section 3.1 softens strong initialization from a requirement for stable convergence to something that facilitates optimization.

D1.justification: New Appendix D provides PyTorch implementations of the original EDM and DDO losses. Appendix C supplies the high-resolution training recipe, noise and learning-rate schedules, evaluation frequency, runtime, and exact autoguidance checkpoint and scale. These substantially expand implementation guidance; the earlier configurations and project-access link are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds explicit RL and f-GAN connections and references for newer generation comparators, while removing the CAF and GDD-I references. Appendix A strengthens its criticism of masked diffusion and adds a qualification for uniform diffusion variants. The central positioning relative to GANs, DPO, and guidance remains intact.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion receive localized revisions, and v2 adds Section 3.4 and a Code Example appendix. Additional Results moves from Appendix D to E through renumbering. Most prose and the overall section sequence are retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds a prominent first-page sample comparison and a 512×512 benchmark table, expands retained tables with parameter-count columns and method groups, and adds curves and adjusts axes in Figure 6. These substantially change the empirical displays. Existing conceptual diagrams and appendix sample grids are retained and renumbered.

improvement.justification: The high-resolution evaluation, broader baselines, continued-MLE control, and loss-code appendix strengthen empirical support and reproducibility beyond v1. The optimizer-state qualification limits the new control's support for the stronger forward-KL interpretation. The revision therefore provides a useful, incremental net quality improvement.
